correctness.rationale: The prefix-count lemma is proved including a single common removable good. Market feasibility is exactly 16 pairwise-split allocations; subjective SD-EF1 depends only on 630 paired rankings per agent. The finite 630² classification produced 96 exceptional classes and the independent full 5040² ranking census produced exactly 6144 incompatible strict profiles, matching the 64-to-1 refinement factor. Both orbit representatives are independently checked against all 128 allocations, their 48-element orbits are disjoint and jointly equal the computed exception set. Assumptions, cardinality normalization, and strict-ranking boundary are explicit.

value.rationale: The seven-good layer is the established first possible nonexistence size in the natural two-agent simultaneous market-and-subjective fairness problem. A complete classification of every minimal obstruction, two nonequivalent types, and exact incidence under uniform rankings are motivated natural finite invariants; they are not routine restatements of the single known witness. The result quantifies generic feasibility and can guide structural sufficient conditions. No larger-market theorem is claimed.
